ui.help_body:
**How to use the app:**

1. Go to **Upload** and select a JPG or PNG image of a maize leaf.
2. The app will automatically analyse the image and switch to **Results**.
3. If a disease is detected, explore the **Overview**, **Prevention**, and **Treatment** tabs.
4. For healthy leaves, the app shows good agronomic practices to maintain crop health.

---

**Tips for accurate results:**
- Use a close-up, well-lit photo of a single maize leaf.
- Avoid blurry, dark, or heavily cropped images.
- The model detects: **Blight**, **Common Rust**, **Gray Leaf Spot**, and **Healthy** leaves.
- Images that don't resemble a maize leaf will be rejected.

healthy_practices: Maintain good agronomic practices and soil health.
Use crop rotation and plant disease-resistant varieties.
Monitor regularly for early signs of pests and disease.
Ensure balanced fertilization and avoid water stress.
Keep field edges and irrigation equipment clean.

blight.description: Refers to several diseases causing large, elongated, cigar-shaped lesions on leaves. Northern Corn Leaf Blight (NCLB) is caused by Setosphaeria turcica and Southern Corn Leaf Blight (SCLB) by Bipolaris maydis. Symptoms worsen in cool, humid conditions.
symptoms: Large, elongated tan or gray cigar-shaped lesions parallel to leaf veins.
Dusty gray appearance on lesions in moist conditions (fungal spores).
Wilting and seedling death in severe SCLB infections.
Severely infected plants lose all leaves, appearing gray and brittle.
prevention: Select maize hybrids with high resistance or tolerance to blight.
Rotate crops to reduce fungal residue in the soil.
Till or manage crop residues that harbor the fungus.
Maintain proper plant spacing for airflow.
treatment_steps: Remove affected leaves carefully to reduce infection spread.
Apply recommended fungicides following label instructions.
Monitor the plant every 2–3 days for new lesions.

common_rust.description: Common rust is caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi, forming reddish-brown pustules that reduce photosynthesis. It thrives in cool, humid conditions and can be identified by initial chlorotic flecks followed by the eruption of powdery spores.
symptoms: Numerous small (1–2 mm), circular to elongated golden-brown to brick-red powdery pustules.
Small yellow spots or flecks appearing before pustules become visible.
Tissue around pustules turns yellow or dies off.
Reduced photosynthesis and overall plant vigour.
prevention: Plant commercially bred hybrid corn with resistance to common rust.
Regularly inspect lower and upper leaves for rust pustules.
Destroy infected crop residue by burning or burying.
treatment_steps: Apply fungicides early when pustules first appear, following label instructions.
Remove and destroy heavily infected plants.
Monitor fields regularly to catch early re-infection.

gray_leaf_spot.description: Gray Leaf Spot (GLS) is caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis or Cercospora zeina. It appears as rectangular tan-to-gray lesions parallel to leaf veins. The disease thrives in warm, humid conditions and overwinters in infected corn residue.
symptoms: Small tan pinpoint spots with yellow halos that develop into narrow rectangular gray lesions.
Lesions delimited by leaf veins, growing up to 2 inches long.
Disease starts on lower leaves and spreads upward through the canopy.
Premature leaf drying and reduced photosynthetic area.
prevention: Plant disease-tolerant or resistant corn hybrids.
Rotate maize with non-host crops for at least one year.
Till soil to incorporate and decompose corn residue.
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness.
Control weeds to improve air circulation.
treatment_steps: Apply recommended fungicides if lesions are actively spreading.
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest.
Maintain optimal plant density for adequate airflow.
